headline: High: Authelia can egress broadly while Botpress can install packages, creating default-path data and workflow risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are otherwise limited by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth outputs and Botpress is an LLM chatbot platform; if operators bridge them via copy-paste or a shared workspace, Botpress could ingest Authelia-generated content as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF operators connect Authelia outputs into Botpress prompts or knowledge sources
IF Botpress treats imported text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Keep Authelia and Botpress in separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of raw auth logs into Botpress
Add a provenance prefix to imported text
Review Botpress prompt templates for instruction delimiters

B_data_leakage.rationale: A leakage path is not documented because neither profile shows a shared filesystem or sensitive data classes. Authelia has broad network egress and Botpress has no egress, so the pair does not obviously exfiltrate by default. Uncertainty remains because both are unverified docs-only profiles, so I avoid claiming stronger isolation than shown.
conditions: IF either agent is configured to process secrets or PII
IF a shared workspace or OAuth principal is introduced
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared folders
Confirm Botpress remains network-disabled
Audit Authelia logs for secret material
Use separate service accounts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make outbound API calls and Botpress can install packages, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git, or shared mutable resource access. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Because the profiles are sparse and unverified, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory or package cache
IF an orchestrator grants shared mutable state
mitigations: Separate package caches
Run each agent under distinct service accounts
Avoid shared writable directories
Document ownership of mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions through OIDC/ForwardAuth, and Botpress is a chatbot/LLM system that may render or act on upstream text. If Botpress consumes Authelia outputs without verification, a mistaken auth-related message can cascade into incorrect user-facing actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, so I choose medium.
conditions: IF Botpress uses Authelia output as authoritative input
IF no verification step checks auth claims before downstream action
mitigations: Insert a validation step before Botpress acts on auth data
Render Authelia outputs as untrusted text
Log and review any auth-driven Botpress actions
Use structured schemas for exchanged messages

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source docs-only entries. The only compliance-relevant signal is Authelia's broad network egress, which could matter if regulated data is routed through it, but Botpress shows no such flow. I therefore keep this low and do not cite only one agent.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Authelia into Botpress
IF deployment policies require residency or retention guarantees not configured here
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Check retention settings on both systems
Document data flow boundaries
Review deployment region settings
